question: Does a human-choice prior speed learning of a NEW goal, and does that depend on the learning rule (PPO vs local three-factor rules)?

rooms.test: 16 fresh confirmation rooms, seeds 1000-1029; room = pair seed%8, A

calibration.rule: max mean final dev success over priors; PPO untuned (registered)

primary.outcome: normalised learning-curve AUC (trapezoid over CURVE of successes/30, divided by 30 x budget) and final success
primary.contrasts: per learner: human_bc - human_legal_uniform, human_bc - cold_ppo (paired over 30 seeds); Holm over the 6 AUC contrasts

secondary: final success; learner contrasts within prior; trapped/revisit at the final probe; dev seeds 1000-1002 also appear in test (different rooms)
caveat: local learners are biologically plausible credit-assignment rules on a backprop-trained (BC+PPO) starting network; not spiking, not a full bio-plausible agent
